title: What a Workflow Does
moduleName: Workflows: An Introduction and Your First Simple Automation
learningGoal: Understand what a workflow is and choose a process that is a good fit for automation.

items.title: Automatic Instructions
items.description: A workflow tells LeadProspectrr what to do after a specific event occurs. It repeats the process in the same order each time.

items.title: Examples
items.description: When someone submits a speaking inquiry form, send a confirmation. When a prospect books a strategy call, send reminders. When a client pays an invoice, send welcome information.

items.title: Characteristics
items.description: One clear starting event. One type of contact. No more than three or four actions. One person responsible for the next human step. A result that is easy to test.

items.title: What to Avoid
items.description: Do not begin with a long process containing many branches, messages, offers, and exceptions. Start with one small job that can fit on one screen.

items.title: Better First Workflow
items.description: A form confirmation that sends one email, adds one tag, and notifies one person. It has one purpose and is easier to test than a complex 90-day sales process.

keyPoint: A workflow repeats a process in the same order each time. You decide the process first, then build the instructions. Start small and simple.

actionSteps.title: Identify a Repeated Task
actionSteps.description: Write down one repeated task that begins after a prospect takes a clear action.

actionSteps.title: Check the Fit
actionSteps.description: Does it have one clear starting event, one contact type, and 3-4 actions?

actionSteps.title: Choose Your First Workflow
actionSteps.description: Pick the simplest, most repeatable task to automate first.

quizzes.question: What is a workflow?

options.option_text: A set of instructions LeadProspectrr follows automatically after a specific event

quizzes.explanation: A workflow is a set of automatic instructions that LeadProspectrr follows when a specific trigger event occurs. It repeats the process consistently each time.

quizzes.question: What makes a good first workflow?

options.option_text: A 90-day sales process with twelve emails and many branches
One clear starting event, one contact type, 3-4 actions, one owner, easy to test

quizzes.explanation: A good first workflow is simple: one clear trigger, one contact type, 3-4 actions, one person responsible, and results that are easy to test.

quizzes.question: What should you avoid as a first workflow?

options.option_text: Long processes with many branches, messages, offers, and exceptions

quizzes.explanation: Avoid complex first workflows with many branches and exceptions. Start with a simple, linear process that fits on one screen.

title: The Building Blocks
moduleName: Workflows: An Introduction and Your First Simple Automation
learningGoal: Recognize the parts of a workflow and the job each part performs.

items.title: 1. Trigger
items.description: The event that starts the workflow. Examples: Form submitted, Appointment booked, Tag added, Payment received, Customer replied.

items.title: 2. Filter
items.description: Narrows the trigger. Without a filter, a workflow may start after every form submission. The filter tells it to respond only to specific events.

items.title: 3. Action
items.description: A task LeadProspectrr completes after the trigger. Examples: Send email, Add tag, Send notification.

items.title: 4. Wait
items.description: Pauses the contact before the next action. Useful for timing follow-up messages or creating delays.

items.title: 5. End Point
items.description: Shows where the process finishes. A booked appointment, reply, payment, or status change may stop further actions.

items.title: 6. Draft and Published
items.description: Draft: saved but does not respond to real triggers. Published: can process contacts who meet trigger rules.

keyPoint: Workflows have six building blocks: Trigger, Filter, Action, Wait, End Point, and Draft/Published status. Each has a specific job in the automation process.

actionSteps.title: Match Items to Jobs
actionSteps.description: Trigger starts, Filter limits, Action does, Wait pauses, End point finishes, Draft/Published controls if it runs.

actionSteps.title: Identify in Examples
actionSteps.description: Look at the example workflows and identify each building block.

actionSteps.title: Plan Your Blocks
actionSteps.description: For your first workflow, which blocks will you need?

quizzes.question: What does a trigger do?
quizzes.explanation: The trigger is the event that starts the workflow. Examples include form submissions, appointment bookings, tag additions, and payments received.

quizzes.question: What is the purpose of a filter?

options.option_text: To limit which events or contacts qualify for the workflow

quizzes.explanation: A filter narrows the trigger so the workflow only responds to specific events or contacts, preventing unwanted workflow runs.

quizzes.question: What is the difference between Draft and Published?

options.option_text: Draft does not respond to real triggers; Published can process qualifying contacts

quizzes.explanation: Draft workflows are saved but inactive. Published workflows actively process contacts who meet the trigger conditions.

title: Map the Process Before Building
moduleName: Workflows: An Introduction and Your First Simple Automation
learningGoal: Turn a real business need into a simple workflow plan.

items.title: 1. What event starts the process?
items.description: Identify the trigger event that should begin the automation.

items.title: 2. Which contact or event should qualify?
items.description: Define the filter criteria to limit who enters the workflow.

items.title: 3. What should happen first, second, third?
items.description: List the actions in order of execution.

items.title: 4. Who owns the next human action?
items.description: Name the person responsible for follow-up after the automation.

items.title: 5. How will you prove it worked?
items.description: Define how you will test and verify the workflow functions correctly.

items.title: What starts it?
items.description: A contact submits the Consultation Inquiry Form.

items.title: Who qualifies?
items.description: Only contacts who submit that exact form.

items.title: What happens?
items.description: First: Send confirmation email. Second: Add tag inquiry-new. Third: Notify business owner.

items.title: Who owns follow-up?
items.description: The business owner or assigned team member.

items.title: How is it tested?
items.description: Submit the form with your own email and check all three results.

items.title: Recommended Pattern
items.description: SOURCE – PURPOSE – MAIN RESULT. Example: FORM – New Inquiry – Confirm + Tag + Notify

items.title: More Examples
items.description: FORM – Speaking Inquiry – Confirm + Notify. FORM – Coaching Application – Tag + Assign. CALENDAR – Strategy Call – Confirm + Remind.

keyPoint: Answer the five planning questions before opening the Workflow Builder. A clear plan makes building faster and reduces errors.

actionSteps.title: Complete the Planner
actionSteps.description: Answer all five planning questions for your first workflow.

actionSteps.title: Name Your Workflow
actionSteps.description: Use the pattern: SOURCE – PURPOSE – MAIN RESULT

actionSteps.title: Review Before Building
actionSteps.description: Make sure your plan is clear and simple before opening the Workflow Builder.

quizzes.question: What are the five planning questions?

options.option_text: What event starts it, who qualifies, what happens, who owns follow-up, how to prove it worked
How much, how many, how long, how often, how far
What color, what size, what shape, what weight, what material

quizzes.explanation: The five planning questions are: What event starts the process? Which contact qualifies? What should happen? Who owns the next action? How will you prove it worked?

quizzes.question: What is the recommended workflow naming pattern?
quizzes.explanation: Use the pattern SOURCE – PURPOSE – MAIN RESULT. Example: FORM – New Inquiry – Confirm + Tag + Notify. This makes workflows easy to identify.

quizzes.question: Why map the process before building?

options.option_text: A clear plan makes building faster and reduces errors

quizzes.explanation: Mapping the process before building creates a clear plan, making construction faster and reducing mistakes. It ensures you know what you want before you start building.

title: Create the Workflow and Trigger
moduleName: Workflows: An Introduction and Your First Simple Automation
learningGoal: Create a blank workflow and connect it to one selected form.

items.title: Navigate to Workflows
items.description: Go to Automations → Workflows. Select Create Workflow. Choose Start from Scratch.

items.title: Name Your Workflow
items.description: Enter the workflow name: FORM – New Inquiry – Confirm + Tag + Notify. Keep it in Draft while building.

items.title: Add New Trigger
items.description: Select Add New Trigger. Search for Form Submitted. Select the trigger.

items.title: Label the Trigger
items.description: Give it a clear name: New Inquiry Form Submitted.

items.title: Filter to Specific Form
items.description: Add filter Form Is. Select the exact inquiry form. Save the trigger.

items.title: Why the Filter Matters
items.description: Without a form filter, other submissions may start the workflow. A specific filter keeps it tied to one business purpose.

keyPoint: Create the workflow in Draft, add a Form Submitted trigger with a specific form filter, and save each step before continuing.

actionSteps.title: Create Workflow
actionSteps.description: Go to Automations → Workflows → Create Workflow → Start from Scratch.

actionSteps.title: Name It Clearly
actionSteps.description: Use the pattern: FORM – New Inquiry – Confirm + Tag + Notify

actionSteps.title: Add Trigger and Filter
actionSteps.description: Add Form Submitted trigger, label it, and filter to your specific form.

actionSteps.title: Check Before Continuing
actionSteps.description: Verify: clear name, correct trigger, clear label, correct form filter, saved trigger, Draft status.

quizzes.question: Where do you create a workflow?
quizzes.explanation: Workflows are created in Automations → Workflows. This is where you build, edit, and manage all automation sequences.

quizzes.question: Why should you keep the workflow in Draft while building?

options.option_text: Draft does not respond to real triggers, so you can build safely

quizzes.explanation: Keeping a workflow in Draft while building prevents it from responding to real trigger events. This lets you build and test safely before going live.

quizzes.question: Why does the Form Submitted trigger need a filter?

options.option_text: It limits the workflow to the selected form and prevents unrelated submissions from starting it

quizzes.explanation: Without a form filter, any form submission could trigger the workflow. The filter ensures only submissions from your specific form start this workflow.

title: Add the Three Actions
moduleName: Workflows: An Introduction and Your First Simple Automation
learningGoal: Add the contact message, contact tag, and team notification in the correct order.

items.title: Add Email Action
items.description: Select + below trigger. Choose Send Email. Enter sender name and connected address. Add subject and message. Save.

items.title: Suggested Email
items.description: Subject: We received your request. Body: Thank you for getting in touch. We received your request and will review it shortly. You can expect to hear from us within [response time].

items.title: Add Tag Action
items.description: Select next +. Choose Add Contact Tag. Select or create inquiry-new. Save.

items.title: Use Consistent Spelling
items.description: Use one spelling for the tag. Small differences create separate tags and make lists harder to manage.

items.title: Add Notification Action
items.description: Select next +. Choose Internal Notification. Select notification method. Choose recipient. Add contact details and response time. Save.

items.title: Suggested Notification
items.description: Subject: New inquiry received. Body: Name, Email, Phone, Next action: Review and respond within [response time].

keyPoint: Add three actions in order: confirmation email, contact tag, internal notification. Save each action and review the full path before testing.

actionSteps.title: Add Confirmation Email
actionSteps.description: Write and save the confirmation email action.

actionSteps.title: Add Contact Tag
actionSteps.description: Add the inquiry-new tag action with consistent spelling.

actionSteps.title: Add Internal Notification
actionSteps.description: Configure who receives the notification and what it says.

actionSteps.title: Review Full Path
actionSteps.description: Check: correct form, accurate email, correct tag spelling, right recipient, all saved.

quizzes.question: What are the three actions in this workflow?

options.option_text: Delete contact, send spam, ignore inquiry
Send confirmation email, add tag inquiry-new, send internal notification
Create invoice, charge payment, ship product

quizzes.explanation: The three actions are: 1) Send a confirmation email to the contact, 2) Add the tag inquiry-new to organize the lead, 3) Send an internal notification to the team.

quizzes.question: Why use consistent tag spelling?

options.option_text: Small differences create separate tags and make lists harder to manage

quizzes.explanation: Consistent tag spelling is crucial. inquiry-new and Inquiry-New would be treated as two different tags, fragmenting your contact organization.

quizzes.question: What should the internal notification include?

options.option_text: Name, email, phone, and expected response time

quizzes.explanation: The internal notification should include the contact's name, email, phone, and the expected response time so the team member has all information needed for follow-up.

title: Test, Inspect, and Correct
moduleName: Workflows: An Introduction and Your First Simple Automation
learningGoal: Run a controlled test and verify each result before real prospects enter the workflow.

items.title: Strongest Test Method
items.description: Publish the workflow briefly and complete the real starting event. Review every step, change to Published, open the form as a visitor, submit with your own details, check contact record and inboxes.

items.title: Result 1: Confirmation Email
items.description: The confirmation email arrived at the test contact's email address.

items.title: Result 2: Contact Tag
items.description: The contact record contains inquiry-new.

items.title: Result 3: Internal Notification
items.description: The internal notification reached the selected person.

items.title: Nothing happened?
items.description: Is the workflow Published?

items.title: Test contact did not enter?
items.description: Did you submit the exact form selected in the trigger?

items.title: Email did not arrive?
items.description: Check sending address, contact email, message setup, and DND status.

items.title: Tag is missing?
items.description: Was the correct tag selected and the action saved?

items.title: Notification missing?
items.description: Check the recipient and notification method.

keyPoint: Test passes only when all three results are correct: confirmation email, contact tag, and internal notification. Check workflow activity and correct one item at a time.

actionSteps.title: Publish Briefly
actionSteps.description: Change workflow to Published for testing.

actionSteps.title: Submit Test Form
actionSteps.description: Use your own name and email to submit the form.

actionSteps.title: Check Three Results
actionSteps.description: Verify: confirmation email arrived, tag was added, notification was sent.

actionSteps.title: Correct and Retest
actionSteps.description: Change one item at a time, save, and repeat the test. Record faults and corrections.

nextLessonTitle: Adapt the Workflow to Your Business

quizzes.question: What is the strongest test method?

options.option_text: Publish briefly and complete the real starting event with your own details
Ask someone else to guess if it works

quizzes.explanation: The strongest test is to publish the workflow briefly and actually submit the form with your own details. This tests the real trigger and all actions in sequence.

quizzes.question: What are the three results to check?

options.option_text: Confirmation email, contact tag inquiry-new, and internal notification

quizzes.explanation: The three-result test checks: 1) Confirmation email arrived, 2) Contact has inquiry-new tag, 3) Internal notification was received. All three must pass.

quizzes.question: What should you do if something fails?

options.option_text: Give up and delete the workflow
Change one item at a time, save, and retest

quizzes.explanation: When troubleshooting, change one item at a time, save it, and repeat the full test. This helps identify exactly what was causing the problem.

title: Adapt the Workflow to Your Business
moduleName: Workflows: An Introduction and Your First Simple Automation
learningGoal: Apply the same workflow pattern to a real process used by your business.

items.title: Scenario A: Coach
items.description: Prospect submits coaching application. Needs receipt message, inquiry-new tag, and notification to coach.

items.title: Scenario B: Consultant
items.description: Business owner requests strategy conversation. Needs confirmation, tag, and notification to consultant.

items.title: Scenario C: Speaker
items.description: Event organizer submits speaking inquiry. Needs confirmation, tag, and notification to booking handler.

items.title: Scenario D: Service Business
items.description: Prospect requests quote. Needs confirmation, tag, and notification to person responsible for estimates.

items.title: 1. Write Trigger Event
items.description: Document the exact event that starts your workflow.

items.title: 2. Name the Form
items.description: Identify the exact form used as the filter.

items.title: 3. Draft Confirmation Email
items.description: Write the message your contacts will receive.

items.title: 4. Name the Owner
items.description: Identify who is responsible for follow-up.

items.title: 5. Set Response Time
items.description: Define expected response time for follow-up.

items.title: 6. Build in Draft
items.description: Create the workflow in Draft status.

items.title: 7. Test and Record
items.description: Test with your details and record results.

items.title: 8. Correct and Retest
items.description: Fix any issues and test again.

items.title: Complete When
items.description: One selected form starts the workflow. Test contact receives confirmation. Contact record gets inquiry-new tag. Correct person receives notification. Workflow activity shows completed path. Named person owns next human action.

items.title: Future Improvements
items.description: Once the first workflow works, you may add: Create follow-up task, Add contact to opportunity pipeline, Wait one business day, Send reminder, End follow-up after appointment booked. Test again after every change.

keyPoint: Apply the same pattern to your real business: one trigger, one filter, three actions, one owner. Complete the exercise and test thoroughly before adding complexity.

actionSteps.title: Choose Your Scenario
actionSteps.description: Pick the scenario closest to your business or create your own.

actionSteps.title: Complete Exercise Steps
actionSteps.description: Work through all eight steps: trigger, form, email, owner, response time, build, test, correct.

actionSteps.title: Reach the Finish Line
actionSteps.description: Ensure all completion criteria are met before considering the workflow done.

quizzes.question: What is the first step in adapting the workflow?

options.option_text: Choose your scenario and write the trigger event

quizzes.explanation: The first step is to choose your scenario and document the exact trigger event that starts your workflow. Planning before building prevents errors.

quizzes.question: What should you do after the first workflow works?

options.option_text: Add one improvement at a time and test again

quizzes.explanation: Once the first workflow works, add improvements one at a time: tasks, pipeline entries, waits, reminders. Test again after every change.

quizzes.question: What is the finish line for this exercise?

options.option_text: The workflow is created in Draft
Form starts workflow, confirmation sent, tag added, notification received, activity shows completion, owner named

quizzes.explanation: The finish line requires: form starts workflow, test contact receives confirmation, inquiry-new tag added, notification received, workflow activity shows completed path, and a named person owns the next action.
